   - `publication_year`: 4-digit year printed on the paper/report itself (e.g. `"2024"`), or `"not reported"` if undated. Give exact page/header in `where_found`.

   - `sample_size`: Exact sample size(s) AND explicit unit(s) of analysis stated in the paper (e.g. `"593 households across 4 neighbourhoods"`, `"128 municipalities; 2,048 observations (2010-2025)"`, `"32 semi-structured interviews"`), or `"not reported"` if pure doctrinal/legal analysis with no empirical sample.
   - `study_design`: Study design as the authors describe it and as operationalized in the methods section (be specific about quantitative/qualitative/quasi-experimental/experimental/review structure).
   - `effect_estimate`: Headline result of the study regarding how the legal, administrative, regulatory, institutional, tenure, tariff/subsidy, or participation factor relates to water/sanitation access/outcomes, with exact printed numbers (point estimates, units, 95% CIs, p-values, sample N) if quantitative, or concise factual headline finding if qualitative (noting `"Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported"` when purely qualitative), in your own words from the paper alone.
   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"` (observational longitudinal cohort study without intervention framing)
     * `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"` (primary qualitative study: interviews, focus groups, ethnography, qualitative case study)
     * `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"` (genuine mixed-methods study combining both qualitative and quantitative primary components)
     * `"AMSTAR 2"` (systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with systematic search/screening; NEVER use for non-systematic narrative literature reviews)
     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)
   - `mechanism_certainty`: Single integer `"0"`, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`, or `"4"` strictly obeying `CODEBOOK.md` §9 and its design ceiling:
     * `"4"` ONLY for randomized trials (`RoB 2`)
     * `"3"` ONLY for `RoB 2` trials OR `ROBINS-I` studies with credible Low/Moderate overall risk of bias
     * All other designs (cross-sectional/JBI, cohort, qualitative/CASP, mixed-methods/MMAT, systematic review/AMSTAR 2, Legal Framework, NONE, or Serious/Critical ROBINS-I) CANNOT exceed `"2"`! (`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).

country.comment: Empirical panel analysis covers prefecture-level cities in urban China.
country.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF p. 3, Introduction; PDF p. 5, Section 'Data and sample'

effect_estimate.comment: 95% CIs are not reported in the paper; exact regression coefficients, clustered standard errors, p-value thresholds, substantive unit conversions, and analytic sample sizes are reported. Non-WASH outcomes also modeled in Table 3 include solid waste treatment capacity (-0.0897 tons/day per 10,000 persons, SE = 0.0268, p < 0.01, N = 1,577), quantity of solid waste treated (-0.00136 [10,000 tons per 10,000 persons], SE = 0.000732, p < 0.1, N = 1,589), and public green space (0.00594 ha per 10,000 persons, SE = 0.0212, non-significant, N = 1,769).
effect_estimate.value: In two-way fixed-effects city-year regressions (2008–2014), a 1-percentage-point increase in temporary residents (migrants without permanent urban hukou registration) is associated with a statistically significant lower municipal wastewater treatment capacity of -0.00164 (10,000 m3/day per 10,000 persons; clustered SE = 0.000529, p < 0.01, N = 1,730 observations across 283 cities), equivalent to -16.4 m3/day per 10,000 persons (-2,460 m3/day for an average sample city of 1.5 million), and a lower annual quantity of wastewater treated of -0.326 (10,000 m3 per 10,000 persons; clustered SE = 0.169, p < 0.1, N = 1,737 observations across 282 cities), equivalent to -3,260 m3/10,000 persons per year. In a cross-sectional 2008–2014 change model, a 1-percentage-point increase in temporary residents is associated with a reduction of 18.0 m3/day per 10,000 persons in wastewater treatment capacity (95% CIs not reported).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 8–10, Section 'Results'; Table 3, PDF p. 9

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 1 (Documented association): the study documents a statistically significant city-level association between the share of urban residents lacking permanent hukou registration and lower per-capita wastewater treatment capacity and volume treated, while explicitly noting on PDF p. 11 that it does not directly observe or unravel the internal administrative/planning causal mechanisms within municipal governments. Also capped at <= 2 by observational non-quasi-experimental study design.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 8–10, Section 'Results'; Table 3, PDF p. 9; PDF p. 11, Section 'Discussion and conclusion'

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines how China's household registration system (hukou documentation/permanent registration eligibility) excludes temporary migrant residents from local governments' accountability scope and municipal urban planning decisions for wastewater treatment infrastructure.

outcome_flags.comment: Measures municipal-level per-capita wastewater treatment plant capacity (10,000 m3/day per 10,000 persons) and annual volume of wastewater treated (10,000 m3 per 10,000 persons per year), capturing aggregate urban sanitation/wastewater infrastructure supply and volumetric treatment quantity rather than household-level drinking water or sewer connection status.

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Observational regression study without a quasi-experimental policy/intervention comparator: the authors deliberately restrict the study period to 2008–2014 prior to the 2014 national hukou reform to avoid policy intervention effects and explicitly describe their models as testing observational correlation between a continuous population share variable and municipal infrastructure outcomes (ruling out ROBINS-I). Because the analysis models contemporaneous city-year secondary statistical indicators (alongside supplementary lagged and cross-sectional change regressions) rather than following an outcome-free epidemiological cohort, JBI Analytical Cross Sectional is selected (JBI Cohort would impose the same mechanism_certainty ceiling of <= 2).
